text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Twenty people have died in the last two days in four villages of Muranga (in central Kenya) after taking a deadly illegal traditionally brewed liquor known as chang'aa, thought to have been laced with a poisonous substance.
- Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka calls on diplomats accredited to Kenya to observe protocol when dealing with issues concerning the country instead of using the press.
- Kenya Human Rights Commission accusses the government of encouraging human rights violations and extra-judicial killings.
- Attorney-General Amos Wako hails non-governmental organisations involved in the fight to eradicate poverty and acceleration of economic growth in the country.
- Cabinet Minister Kipkalia Kones dismisses claims by Stanley Metto, chairman of the giant milk company Kenya Cooperative Creameries chairman, that he is shielding those who looted the cooperative.

- Kenyan permanent representative to U.N. Environment Programme Professor Sam Ongeri says Kenya has had an outstanding performance in the fight against ozone-depleting substances compared to most developing countries.

- Kenyan international mediator Professor Washington Jalang'o Okumu dismisses calls for urgent constitutional reforms, saying that there is not time for a comprehensive review before the next general election.

- The two warring opposition FORD-Kenya (Forum for the Restoration of Democracy) factions are locked up in a battle over the alleged theft of a document drafted on its party policy and which was to serve as a major campaign tool.
